Here is the Title: 🚀 prompt engineering guide, Body: Reader,

Do you, like Brother Elon, think AI poses a threat?

Are you scared the robots are going to take over and dominate us like in the Terminator?

Don't be.

Or, better yet.

Be more like Arnold and be back to terminate those mofos.

Imagine mastering a skill so powerful that it can multiply your results tenfold, transforming your business overnight.

Sounds like a fairytale, right?

But this isn't fantasy—it's the world of prompt engineering techniques.

Let me break it down for you.

Everything in AI starts with a prompt.

Whether it's one-shot, few-shot, chaining, or the tree of thoughts, these techniques are the secret sauce that can turbocharge your AI's performance.

One-shot learning is like a master chef whipping up a gourmet dish from a single glance at the ingredients.

With just one example, you can train your model to understand complex tasks. Imagine the time you'll save!

Few-shot learning is your business’s shortcut to scaling.

By showing the AI a handful of examples, it becomes a pro at the task at hand. It's like hiring a genius employee who only needs minimal training.

And then there's chaining.

This technique is like setting up a series of dominoes—each prompt builds on the last, creating a cascade of insights and solutions. It’s perfect for tackling complex problems in a structured way.

But what about the tree of thoughts?

Think of it as a brainstorming session with your smartest friends, where every idea branches out into multiple possibilities.

It allows your AI to explore different paths and find the most effective solution, ensuring you’re always a step ahead.

Your most valuable asset is time, and these techniques are all about optimizing it.

Stop wasting months trying to piece together the puzzle. Instead, leverage these prompt engineering methods to unlock unprecedented growth and efficiency.

​Get my NEWEST free eBook here.​

It covers these techniques and much more.

The future waits for no man.

Take action now.

And we’ll see you on the other side.

Best, Sabri

P.S. Want to dive deeper? Check out my new free ebook on mastering prompt engineering techniques. It’s packed with actionable insights that will take your business to the next level. Don’t miss out!

Here is the Title: 💡 OpenAI is too Vanilla, Body: Reader,

Last week, I hit up an event for startups, and guess what the main topics were?

AI and Crypto.

Yep, Crypto Bros rubbing shoulders with AI nerds.

Absolute heaven, right?

One session was packed to the rafters, featuring the Chief Architect of OpenAI.

Now, while the session was informative, it was a bit... Vanilla.

No jaw-dropping, game-changing revelations.

But it did cover some solid ground.

Here's the lowdown:

1. Text Models are King: For the foreseeable future, text models will lead the pack. First, it’s text, then pictures, audio, and finally, video. The best models will be text-based.
2. Customization is Key: The market will zero in on customization. While ChatGPT, Gemini, and the like provide general answers, the future lies in customized bots. Think niche-specific AI for tasks like exercises, Q&A, social media, etc. Tons of startups at the event were all about customized GPTs or RAG architecture.
3. The Rise of Multimodality: We're spoiled, really. We expect to interact with our devices using voice, text, video—whatever's convenient at the moment. If it is on our phone, we want to tap it. And that’s the direction AI products are heading. Whether you’re walking down the street or sitting at your desk, your AI should be ready to respond.

My takeaway from the event?

AI will make copying everything easier.

Want to clone Slack or Airbnb? Piece of cake.

But it’s tough to copy something customized, built from your unique data and business insights.

That’s your moat.

Build your own databases, leverage your proprietary information, and create tools that are distinctly yours.

That’s how you stay ahead of the pack.

So, what’s your take on the AI-first world? What’s your strategy to stand out?

To our non-artificial relationship,

Diogo
